brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex base unit: half base piece at (-1,0,0), full bases at (0,0,0) and (1,0,0), with full bases stacked at (0,0,1) and (1,0,1) as shelf levels. Covers/caps closed the open faces (capOpenFaces) and lockJoints applied. check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.
Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at cell 0,1,0 and hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at cell 1,-1,0), each filling an empty position between two touching bases.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only and has no load rating. Load depends on the printed material, infill and joints, which I cannot verify here. No props (books) were added, so no load was modelled. The shelves are plain base tops with no tested capacity.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-base shelf unit with two drawers: a row of three bases on the ground level, two bases stacked on top as shelves, and two notch drawer frames in the empty positions beside them. Caps and joint bolts are applied and the check is clean. The 50 kg rating is not something the configurator can verify, so that requirement is unmet. Before relying on it, the unit would need a material and load test by the user.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
